previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of morbid obesity, COPD, chronic diastolic heart failure, obstructive sleep apnea, and tobacco use was admitted for hypoxia and altered mental status. She presented with respiratory failure likely due to a COPD exacerbation, volume overload from heart failure, and possible infection. She was intubated briefly due to increased work of breathing and required ICU care for oxygen support and monitoring. Treatment included IV diuretics, antibiotics initially for suspected pneumonia later narrowed to COPD exacerbation, and systemic steroids. A urinary tract infection was suspected due to positive initial culture but ruled out on repeat testing. She improved with treatment, regained mental clarity, and was transitioned to oral medications and nebulized bronchodilators. She was discharged to extended care with instructions to use oxygen, CPAP nightly, and nicotine patches to aid smoking cessation, with close monitoring for weight gain and respiratory symptoms.

=======================
Acute Issues:
=======================

# Dyspnea: Patient presented from rehab with a history of 
increased sputum production, wheezing and ""tightness"". She had 
no radiographic findings of PNA, no fevers and no growth on 
sputum or bronch to indicate pneumonia.  The patient did have 
some pulmonary edema. We believe her presentation is primarily 
secondary to COPD exacerbation withi a component of acute on 
chronic CHF exacerbation.  She was initially comvered w/ HCAP 
coverage antibiotics, given solumedrol and nebs.  She was 
maintained on non-invasive pressure support for ~6 hours, then 
required intubation for work of breathing.  Intubation was 
difficult with mildly traumatic initial intubation attempt, 
large neck, and ?laryngeal edema.  Patient was maintained on 
mechanical ventilation for 4 days, and extubated on ___ 
without difficulty.  The patient is maintained on nasal cannula, 
but does have some inspiratory wheeze, which we have asked ENT 
to evaluate. We diuresed with 120mg IV BID of lasix and 5mg of 
metolazone, with good effect.  Pulmonary edema has improved. 
Patient is on Day 5 of prednisone therapy, we were planning for 
a 10d prednisone course. Patient was counseled to discontinue 
smoking, as it is exacerbating her lung disease, causing her 
lung disease.  She plans to quit.  She has a nicotine patch. 

# Community Acquired Pneumonia: Pateint was intially treated for 
HCAP on admission with vanc/cefepime/azithro x 4 days. BAL was 
performed without bacterial growth and no legionella was 
isolated. Patient was transitioned to levaquin for presumed CAP. 
CURB 65 of 3 on admission, however no improved to 2. Completed 
levaquin course and was weaned of supplemental O2. Afebrile for 
the remainder of course. Leukocytosis stable and secondary to 
steroid burst.

# COPD exacerbation: Will need to complete Steroid and 
antibiotic course. FEV1 31% predicted making her Gold Stage III. 
Bicarb chronically elevated ___ to severe COPD. Patient not on 
home ___ and inhaled corticosteroid. Patient was given a 
prednisone burst of 40mg for 9 days, and was treated 
symptomatically with albuterol/ipratroprium nebs. Supplemental 
O2 with goal of 87-93% was maintained to prevent hypercapnia and 
AMS and patient noted to tolerate Rooom air prior to discharge. 
Patient was started on Advair to optomize her COPD treatment 
Longitudinal discussion regarding smoking cessation should be 
performed as an outpatient.

#Leukocytosis: Relatively unchanged from prior days, likely ___ 
to steroid use as patient s/p treatment and clinically improved 
without signs of infection. Would expect to normalize in 
upcoming days.

# Acute Kidney injury: Baseline creatnine of 0.8 with increase 
to 1.4 and BUN elevated to 65 in the setting of diuresis of ~4L 
over 2 days. Likely pre-renal and secondary to over diuresis. 
Clinically sypmotomatic with hypotension and increased thirst 
suggesting intravascular volume depletion. Patient was given 1.5 
L of IVF in ICU prior to transfer and VSS remained stable during 
hospital course. Diureseis was held prior to discharge and 
creatnine improved to 1.0. Lisinopril was initially held but 
restarted prior to discharge.
============================
Chronic Issues:
============================ 

# Acute on chronic diastolic CHF.  EF 55% in ___, thought 
to be due to heart failure with preserved EF. Initially tried to 
diurese with 120mg IV lasix without much effect to added 
metolazone 5mg qd with good effect.  Cr bumped on ___, and 
transiently hypotensive to SBP ___, quickly responsive to 500cc 
IVF, most likely secondary to a component of over-diuresis.  
Patient's metoprolol has been held for bradycardia and 
hypotension. Lisinopril has also been held for relative 
hypotension, but restarted prior to discharge. 

# NIDDM: Likely secondary to solumedrol/prednisone burst. 
Patient was initially treated with insulin drip for first day in 
the MICU, then transitioned to regular insulin sliding scale and 
lantus qhs. Metformin was held in house. When patient started 
taking POs, we transitioned sliding scale to humalog at meals. 
She had incrased insulin needs in the setting of steroids, but 
this became more controlled. She was transitioned back to 
metformin on discharge.

# CAD: Unclear her indication for plavix and ASA, as most recent 
cath was years ago. Discussed with PCP who was not entirely 
clear. We continued ASA and held plavix. Statin was continued. 
Beta blocker and lisinopril were initially held due to 
hypotension but restarted prior to discharge. 

# HTN: Lisinopril initially held, but restarted prior to 
discharge. Patient remained normotensive on medical floor

# Atrial fibrillation: Rate control adequate in ___ to ___, 
occasional PVCsnoted. Patient was initially continued on low 
dose metoprolol but held in setting of hypotension. This was 
restarted prior to discharge as heart rate and BP remained 
stable.

# OSA: Patient refusing CPAP at night. She was placed on 
telemetry for continuous oxygen monitoring and placed on 
supplemental O2 maintaining O2 sats 84-94% overnight.

# Upper airways adventitial sounds: Patient seen and cleared by 
ENT and noted to be due to upper tracheal vs subglottic stenosis 
from hx trach, and thought to be exacerbated by 
suppraglottic/upper tracheal edema from recent intubation 
leading to change in respiratory sounds. No need for additional 
steroids needed. 

Transitional issues: 
[]Currently full code and formal discussion of code status 
should be conducted with PCP.
[] HCP is daughter (not usually available)
[] Longitudinal discussion regarding smoking cessation should be 
performed as an outpatient
[] Patient with CHADS 2 of 3 currently rate controlled with 
metoprolol. Consideration of anticoagulation should be assessed 
by PCP
[] Patient started on fluticasone-salmeterol to optomize COPD 
management.
[] Patient to follow up with pulmonology in 2 weeks.
[] Plavix discontinued as no indication for dual anti-platelet 
therapy and risk of bleeding.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___:

It was a pleasure taking care of you during your hospitalization 
at ___. You had come in because you were experiencing 
increased SOB, and you were found to have very low oxygen 
saturations. We believe that this was due to pneumonia and a 
COPD exacerbation. Since you were having a very difficult time 
breathing you were taken to ICU and intubated so that a machine 
could breath for you. You were given antibiotics and your lungs 
were examined and sample was taken which did not grow any 
dangerous bacteria. You completed 7 days of antibiotics and 
you're breathing began to improve. You were also noted ot have 
an exacerbation of your diastolic heart failure. You were 
diuresed to remove the fluid from your lungs. Your breathing 
tube was removed afterwards and you were transferred to the 
floor where you continued to improve with steroids. You were 
able to breath comfortably on room air prior to discharge but we 
still recommend home oxygen, especially at night, as you have 
refused CPAP. We recommend you stop smoking as this will improve 
your lung function and help prevent these exacerbations in the 
future. Please weigh yourself every morning, call MD if weight 
goes up more than 3 lbs.

We have made the following changes to your medication list:
Please START taking Fluticasone-Salmeterol diskus (advair) 
240/40 1 INH IH BID to help treat your COPD.
Please STOP taking Clopidogrel 75mg PO daily as this medication 
is no longer needed. 
Please CONTINUE taking the rest of your medications as 
prescribed.

Please follow up with your appointments as outlined below.

Thank you,
